clue.text: Strike engulfing university provided opportunity finally for Grace

indicators.note: engulfing means the word for strike swallows the university letter inside it

parts.note: to strike is to beat
provided means if, as in 'provided it rains'

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word opportunity

explanation.surface: A sporting chance for Grace, perhaps W.G. Grace, after a university strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grace' looks like a name but is a verb: to grace something is to adorn it. 'engulfing' puts U inside BEAT, making BEAUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To grace a room is to adorn it or make it more attractive, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Animal hubby's trained to eat bran regularly …

indicators.note: to eat means the rearranged letters take the others inside them
trained means schooled into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
regularly takes every other letter of bran

explanation.surface: A husband's pet has been trained to eat bran, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' looks like it describes the hubby teaching the pet, but it is the anagram signal; 'regularly' picks every other letter of bran.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushbaby is a small nocturnal African primate with large eyes, also called a galago.

clue.text: … notice last month becoming fully grown

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
ult., short for ultimo, means of last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue: a notice saying the pet became fully grown last month.
explanation.walkthrough: ULT is short for ultimo, used in formal letters to mean last month.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult is a person or animal that has reached full maturity.

clue.text: A little concert here, Saturday in May perhaps

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small concert here on a Saturday, perhaps in the month of May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the month but is Theresa May, the former UK Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is the first name of former British Prime Minister Theresa May.

clue.text: Chance of charity event being broadcast

indicators.note: being broadcast means spoken aloud on air, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

parts.note: a fete is an outdoor fundraising fair

explanation.surface: The chance of a charity event being shown on air.
explanation.walkthrough: A fete is a British outdoor fair, often raising money for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Fate is the unseen force or luck that decides what happens.

clue.text: Friends role some egomaniac in Omaha rejected?

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are turned back to front
some says only part of the letters of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters run from the end of egomaniac through in and into Omaha

explanation.surface: Asks whether an egomaniac in Nebraska turned down a part in the sitcom Friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ACINOM from 'egomaniAC IN OMaha', and 'rejected' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Monica Geller is one of the six main characters in the American sitcom Friends.

clue.text: Play the cello, leaving church after orchestra's leader

indicators.note: after means the rest follows the orchestra letter
leader means the opening letter of the word orchestra's
leaving means the church letters depart from the word cello

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for Church of England

explanation.surface: An instruction to play the cello once the orchestra's leader has left church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like an instruction but is the definition. 'leaving' removes CE from CELLO, giving LLO.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is Shakespeare's tragedy of the Moor of Venice.

clue.text: Current Pope, harsh?

parts.note: in means current or fashionable
Clement was the name of fourteen popes

explanation.surface: Asks whether the present Pope is harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement, a name meaning merciful, is ironic here beside harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclement means severe or unkind, most often of stormy weather.

clue.text: Agrees to dispose of new property

indicators.note: to dispose of means getting rid of the new letter

parts.note: assents means agrees

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to sell off a new piece of property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dispose of' sounds like selling the property but removes N from ASSENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are the things a person or firm owns that have value, its property.

clue.text: Hat turned round actor Timothy wore ultimately

indicators.note: round means the word for turned goes around the other pieces

parts.note: milk that has turned has gone sour
Timothy West was a British actor

indicators.note: ultimately takes the closing letter of the word wore

explanation.surface: A hat that actor Timothy West wore, turned round on his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reads like a verb on the hat but means gone off, as milk turns. Timothy West was a well-known British stage and screen actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sou'wester is a waterproof hat with a broad brim at the back, worn by sailors in storms.

clue.text: Endlessly deny describing good Europeans as asylum seekers

indicators.note: describing means drawing a line round, so the shortened word encloses the others
endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to refuse is to deny
E is the abbreviation for European, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A call to stop endlessly denying that asylum seekers are good Europeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense, drawing a line around something, so it signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Refugees are people who have fled their country, often applying for asylum elsewhere.

clue.text: German product son pawns

parts.note: hock is a German white wine from the Rhine
S is the genealogy abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A German product that a son pawns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pawns' looks like chess pieces but is a verb. Hock is a British name for Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To hock something is informal for pawning it, leaving it with a pawnbroker for a loan.

clue.text: Bookie's client now recovered from illness

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in improved health again

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's customer who has got over an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The bookie's client is one who bets; the spelling better is an accepted variant of bettor.
explanation.definitionFit: A punter placing wagers is a better, and someone no longer sick is said to be better.

clue.text: Loaded waste differently at first

indicators.note: differently at first says the opening letter of the word for waste is changed to another

parts.note: effluent is liquid waste

explanation.surface: Waste loaded in a different way at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' is the definition, slang for rich. Change the first letter of EFFLUENT from E to A.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for very wealthy, the same as affluent.

clue.text: Singer James is in France, getting most outspoken

parts.note: James Blunt is an English singer-songwriter
est is French for is

explanation.surface: The singer James Blunt, in France, becoming very frank.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun is that the singer's surname itself means frank.
explanation.definitionFit: Blunt means frank and direct, so the bluntest person speaks most plainly.

clue.text: Bird eagle can rob so cunningly

indicators.note: cunningly says the letters of the preceding words are craftily rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird that an eagle can rob so cunningly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunningly' rearranges EAGLE CAN ROB SO.
explanation.definitionFit: The barnacle goose is a black and white goose breeding in the Arctic and wintering in northern Europe.

clue.text: Mars employee's start in factory, succeeding Ruby, say

indicators.note: succeeding means the factory piece follows the colour

parts.note: ruby is a shade of red

indicators.note: in means the opening letter goes inside the factory word

parts.note: a plant is a factory

indicators.note: start takes the opening letter of employee's

explanation.surface: A Mars confectionery employee starts work at the factory, taking over from someone called Ruby.
explanation.walkthrough: Mars looks like the chocolate company, but it is the planet. 'in' puts E inside PLANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is known as the Red Planet because iron oxide on its surface gives it a reddish colour.

clue.text: Lady true about reason for divorce

indicators.note: about here means turned around and mixed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lady is truthful about the grounds for her divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but rearranges LADY TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Adultery, sex outside marriage, is a traditional legal ground for ending a marriage.

clue.text: Agitated dreading test, I went to pieces

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A nervous examinee says they cracked up while dreading a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitated' looks like the speaker's mood but signals rearranging DREADING TEST I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that disintegrated broke up into fragments, literally falling apart.

clue.text: Expression of defiance from drunk present

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A defiant retort from a drunk who is present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' is a noun here, a sot.
explanation.definitionFit: 'So there!' is a childish retort said to assert oneself or defy someone.

clue.text: Give ground shelter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to withdraw or back away
second meaning: a quiet, secluded refuge

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it suggests donating land for a shelter; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An army in retreat withdraws, and a country retreat is a peaceful hideaway.

clue.text: Unknown flier briefly seen crossing area in capital

indicators.note: crossing means the pieces straddle the area letter, which sits between them

parts.note: Z is a typical algebraic unknown

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: An unknown flying object briefly seen crossing an area of a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests a plane or UFO, but it is a water bird; algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Zagreb is the capital city of Croatia.

clue.text: Excited in anticipation of something 12 will have?

definitions.text: Excited in anticipation of something 12 will have?

parts.words: Excited in anticipation of something 12 will have?
parts.note: 12 across is a person who bets, and what such a punter has is a small wager, whose slang name also describes a nervously excited heart

explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as A + a British slang word for a small bet, which a better (12 across) has; together the letters also mean nervously excited.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a state of nervous excitement has a fluttering heart, like a punter awaiting a race result.

clue.text: Left many heading west over river for walk

indicators.note: over here means the reversed letters lie over the river letter, taking it inside them
in an across answer heading west means reading right to left

parts.note: lots means many
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone left many people behind, heading west over a river on a walk.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer, 'heading west' means reading right to left; the river letter then goes inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is a leisurely, unhurried walk.

clue.text: Board requiring agreement from both Paris and Munich

parts.note: oui is French for yes, as said in Paris
ja is German for yes, as said in Munich

explanation.surface: A board that needs approval from both a French and a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: The board's name really is French yes plus German yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ouija board is a lettered board used in seances to receive supposed spirit messages.

clue.text: Upside-down cakes and squash

indicators.note: in a down answer upside-down means the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: buns are small cakes

explanation.surface: Upside-down cakes and a squash drink, like a baking menu.
explanation.walkthrough: Upside-down cake is a real dessert, which hides the reversal; squash is a soft drink in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub someone is to rebuff them, squashing them with a put-down.

clue.text: Variety of peeled fruits …

indicators.note: peeled means the outer skin is removed, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: oranges are fruits

explanation.surface: A selection of peeled fruits, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peeled' strips the outer letters O and S from ORANGES.
explanation.definitionFit: A range of goods is a variety or assortment of them.

clue.text: … fruit that's brown and green cultivated across Italy

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: across means the rearranged letters reach over either side of the Italy letter
cultivated means worked or tilled, so the letters of green are reworked

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue: a brown and green fruit grown in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' fits the fruit-growing picture but signals an anagram of the colour green.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small, loose-skinned citrus fruit like a mandarin.

clue.text: Swimmer needs time during dependency treatment to reflect

indicators.note: to reflect is to mirror, so the letters are read backwards
during means the time letter sits inside the word for treatment

parts.note: rehab is treatment for drug or alcohol dependency

explanation.surface: A swimmer needs time to think things over during addiction treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reflect' looks like pondering but signals reversal. 'during' puts T in REHAB, giving REHTAB, then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bather is someone who swims or bathes, especially in the sea.

clue.text: Telegraph piece unread by its subject?

definitions.text: Telegraph piece unread by its subject?

parts.words: Telegraph piece unread by its subject?
parts.note: a newspaper article about someone who has died, which that person can never read

explanation.walkthrough: The Telegraph is the very newspaper carrying the puzzle; its subject cannot read the piece because they are dead.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is a newspaper notice of a death with an account of the person's life.
